overall: Atlanta is already at 87.8°F by 10:50 ET with a strong warming rate of +3.6°F/hr, indicating the day is running ahead of a typical June warming curve. The high dewpoint of 69.8°F adds humidity-driven heat load, and the temperature trend from 78.8°F at 7am to 87.8°F by 10:50am reflects consistent, unimpeded heating. With peak heating typically arriving around 3–4 PM ET, significant additional warming remains ahead.
forecast_obs_notes: The deterministic models cluster in two groups — GFS and HRRR both at 92.1°F and ECMWF and NBM both at 90.0°F — showing moderate spread of ~2°F but general agreement that the high will land in the low 90s. Notably, the ensemble signals flagging 87–88°F and 90–91°F as low-probability Tier 4 bins are already being challenged by the observed 87.8°F running max at 10:50am, suggesting the ensemble tails may be underdispersed on the high end today.
max_temp_prediction: With 87.8°F already locked in at 10:50am and roughly 4 hours of peak heating remaining, the daily high is very likely to reach the 90–92°F range. The +3.6°F/hr velocity, even if it decelerates toward 1–2°F/hr through the afternoon, is consistent with a final max near 91°F, aligning with the midpoint of the GFS/HRRR (92.1°F) and ECMWF/NBM (90.0°F) spread. Confidence is moderate-to-high that the max lands between 90 and 92°F, with 91°F as the best single estimate.
